A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Product of Experts research. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable, and retained content can be matched across substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-insertion and video-generation evaluations in Tables 1 and 2, plus text-to-image and autoregressive-video experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds character-insertion, MIG-Bench layout-generation and quantitative sampling-ablation results.

M1.justification: The core sampler in Algorithm 1 is retained. v2 adds a layout-control instantiation using regional FLUX-Depth experts conditioned on 3DIS-generated depth, with summed global and regional VQA rewards (Appendix E.5). This is a bounded procedural adaptation beyond v1's text-only regional composition. The autoregressive construction already existed in v1 Appendix C.

E1.justification: v2 adds character insertion using 80 background-character combinations from Magic Insert and explicit layout-conditioned generation on 50 MIG-Bench scenes. These expand the evaluated object population and control-input scenarios. The original graphics-engine, object-centric video, PhysGen3D and illustrative text-to-image evaluations remain.

E2.justification: The new character comparison evaluates Magic Insert, Add-it, FLUX-Fill and SDEdit (Table 1), while the layout comparison adds 3DIS-FLUX (Table 3). Original comparators remain. FramePack's appearance in the main text is a relabeling and relocation of the earlier autoregressive comparison, not a new baseline.

E3.justification: v2 introduces character-placement and preprocessing procedures, random selection of 50 of 800 MIG-Bench scenes, GroundingDINO bounding-box mIoU, global/regional VQA evaluation, and particle budgets extending to L=32. It also adds SAM2-based foreground IoU to the retained object-centric video evaluation. These are new evaluation protocols and metrics, rather than merely additional setting disclosures.

E4.justification: v1's conditional-sampling ablation and illustrative composition/particle comparisons are retained. v2 adds systematic quantitative particle scaling and SMC-on/off comparisons at matched particle counts, with runtime measurements (Tables 3 and 4). These directly examine whether intermediate resampling improves results beyond increasing the candidate budget.

E5.justification: v2 retains the mean-plus-minus reporting format but removes v1 Table 1's explicit statement that ± denotes standard deviation, without supplying an equivalent explanation. Neither version reports a repeated-run count or significance-testing protocol; additional result rows do not establish additional independent runs.

E6.justification: All retained numerical entries in Tables 1 and 2 are unchanged. v2 adds character-insertion scores, video foreground IoUs, and layout/SMC results. For example, Table 3 reports mIoU 0.728 and VQAScore 0.904 for L=32 versus 0.673 and 0.800 for 3DIS-FLUX. Table 4 shows semantic benefits from SMC but mixed small-budget mIoU effects. These are newly reported comparisons, not performance gains over v1 under identical settings.

T1.justification: v2 Appendix C.1 corrects the velocity-to-score conversion from v1 Appendix D.1 with an algebraically different expression, changing the schedule-dependent coefficients. The product-distribution definitions, conditional-independence assumption and conditional-sampling argument remain. The endpoint-prediction formula is relocated rather than newly derived.

C1.justification: v2 drops v1's concluding assertion of generating outputs with higher complexity and focuses the stated benefits on controllability and fidelity. This is a limited narrowing; the central claims of training-free heterogeneous expert composition and efficient annealed/SMC sampling remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations of character-insertion failures, including SDEdit's background changes from global noising, and interprets the layout results as reducing the need for application-specific attention interventions. Table 4 additionally interprets SMC as improving sampling efficiency with little overhead. Appendix B's limitations concerning computation, incompatible experts and small expert counts are retained.

D1.justification: v2 documents SAM2 segmentation, GPT o4-mini captions, character placement, SDEdit noise strength, layout-depth construction, regional rewards and new experiment hyperparameters (Appendices E.3–E.5), plus particle-dependent runtimes. Conversely, v1's detailed GPT-o1-mini text-to-layout recipe and specific video-checkpoint links disappear despite retention of those demonstrations. Reproducibility information changes substantially in both directions.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning through historical product-distribution and MRF/CRF work and contemporary composition methods. Section 2 now specifically distinguishes its per-timestep MCMC approach from the path-wise importance weighting attributed to Skreta et al. and He et al. It also adds literature supporting the new benchmarks and comparators; these changes go beyond citation formatting.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and sampling exposition are extensively rewritten. Implementation details move from the main text into Appendix E.1, autoregressive experiments move into Section 4.2, and the original text-to-image demonstration moves into Appendix D.5. The experimental narrative and appendix organization are substantially restructured.

P2.justification: v2 expands Tables 1 and 2, adds Tables 3 and 4 and character/layout comparison Figures 6 and 8, and redesigns the PhysGen3D gallery. Retained autoregressive and text-to-image figures are relocated and reformatted, while Figures 1 and 3 lose illustrative rows. Document-wide typography, headers and layout also change substantially.

improvement.justification: v1 supported its text-to-image composition and sampling-efficiency claims mainly through selected examples. v2 adds a 50-scene benchmark, matched particle/resampling controls and runtimes, making those claims substantially more assessable (Tables 3 and 4). The character-insertion comparison broadens validation against relevant methods, and the score-conversion correction improves mathematical accuracy. Lost reproduction details and the missing uncertainty definition are real regressions, but the stronger empirical support provides a substantial net improvement.
